advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit a visible paused signal (summary/notice) whenever result['state']=='paused' even if the stderr marker fails to parse, rather than silently skipping annotation.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_bridge_commands.py:259: `if payload is not None:` — the else branch is silent (no summary, no notice)

_pause_payload requires `tuple(payload) == keys` (exact key set AND order) at line 224, coupling visibility to the emitter's literal dict order in rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:189-194; any drift silently disables the annotation
Litmus: in the world 'paused but marker not parseable', the visibility check produces nothing — indistinguishable from 'paused and correctly annotated' vs the pre-fix silent-green run
advisory.finding: When result['state']=='paused' but _pause_payload() returns None (marker absent, malformed, duplicated, or its JSON key order drifts from the emitter), no step summary and no ::notice:: are written, so a paused no-op run reverts to an ordinary green run with no visible signal — the exact defect this ticket fixes. The paused state is a definite signal available in result['state'], but the visible marker is only emitted when a second, fragile stderr re-parse succeeds; the guard cannot distinguish 'paused and annotated' from 'paused but annotation silently skipped'.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the `state=='paused'` branch, when `_pause_payload` returns None still write a degraded notice/summary (e.g. 'Reconcile Bridge paused; pause detail unavailable') so a paused run is never indistinguishable from a successful reconcile.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Escape or fence the interpolated reason/who values (e.g. strip newlines and backticks, or use a fenced block) before writing them into the GitHub step summary.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:319-322: `bridge_pause(reason: str ...)` only rejects empty/blank reasons; any other string content is accepted verbatim
payload['reason'] flows unmodified through _pause_payload (only type/non-empty checks) into the code span
advisory.finding: The operator-controlled pause `reason` (and `who`) are interpolated verbatim into a Markdown code span in the GitHub step summary. bridge_pause() accepts any non-empty string as `reason`, so a value containing a backtick or newline breaks out of the `` `...` `` span and injects arbitrary Markdown into the operator-facing summary.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that the paused run emits the `::notice title=Reconcile Bridge paused` annotation to stderr.
evidence: Added lines: 'sys.stderr.write("::notice title=Reconcile Bridge paused::No reconciliation ran; " "see the job summary for the pause reason.\n")'
search for '::notice' in tests/scripts returned (no matches)
test_exact_pause_marker_is_benign_and_skips_delivery (tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py:52-74) asserts only summary_text content, never completed.stderr for the notice
advisory.finding: The `::notice title=Reconcile Bridge paused::...` stderr annotation emitted on a paused run (newly added) is not asserted by any test; a regression that dropped or changed the notice text would go undetected.
scenarios: Refactor or typo silently removes the GitHub Actions notice annotation; operators lose the log-annotation signal but tests stay green
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_exact_pause_marker_is_benign_and_skips_delivery, add: assert "::notice title=Reconcile Bridge paused::" in completed.stderr
